title.text: Workflow mapping (practical)

objects.text: Which of my tasks should be a rule, an AI step or an agent?

Applied AI and Automation  |  Session 12 of 14
KLAi Professional Learning  |  Jotham Martin Wambi

slides.notes:
Welcome to Session 12, the first of three practical sessions. For eleven sessions I mostly demonstrated and you watched. Today you work on one task of your own, from work or the summary of your own email. We map it, decide what kind of help each step needs, and estimate the hours you could save.

The question for today is this: Which of my tasks should be a rule, an AI step or an agent? Keep it in mind. At the end of the session we come back to it and see how much more you can say.

title.text:
Your two hours: 55 minutes
are your own workflow

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_plan_11.90x3.95_996f2b5b.png
objects.alt: The two hours in parts, in minutes

objects.text: Most of today is your own work, with me at your side.

slides.notes:
This is the first practical. Twenty minutes on the idea: how to map a workflow and decide, step by step, between a rule, an AI step, an agent and a person. Fifteen minutes of demonstration: a recorded AI sort and a simple keyword rule, side by side on the same twelve messages.

Then fifty-five minutes on your own workflow, from work or from your own email. We end with a decision on what to build first.

title.text: Three questions from last time

runs.text: 1.  What are the three steps of the agent loop?
2.  Which four kinds of action must always pass the approval gate?
3.  What are the four rows of the Tool Boundary Sheet?

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_question_2.80.png

objects.text: Answer aloud first. Then we check together.

slides.notes:
Three quick questions from Session 11. Answer aloud first, and then we check together. It is a warm-up to bring last time back.

Question one. What are the three steps of the agent loop? Take a moment.

A good answer is this. Plan the next step, act by calling one tool, observe the result, and repeat until the goal is met or a stop condition fires.

Question two. Which four kinds of action must always pass the approval gate? Say it to yourself first.

A good answer is this. Sends, payments, deletions and commitments such as accepting a price.

Question three. What are the four rows of the Tool Boundary Sheet? Think about your own task as you answer.

A good answer is this. Read, write, send and spend. For each: what it may do, what a person approves and what it must never do.

If an answer was missing, your own task card or last workbook page has it. Now to today.

title.text: Words we use today

rows.text: A task that repeats, from the event that starts it to the result someone checks.
The event that starts a workflow, such as a message arriving.
The moment work passes from one person or system to another. Errors and delays gather here.
How long the task takes and how often it goes wrong today, measured before you change anything.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_gear_0.70.png
/Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_bell_0.70.png
/Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_people_0.70.png
/Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_clock_0.70.png

slides.notes:
Four words for today. I give the plain meaning of each, and we use every one of them before the end of the session.

Workflow. A task that repeats, from the event that starts it to the result someone checks.

Trigger. The event that starts a workflow, such as a message arriving.

Handoff. The moment work passes from one person or system to another. Errors and delays gather here.

Baseline. How long the task takes and how often it goes wrong today, measured before you change anything.

title.text:
Every workflow has four parts: a
trigger, steps, handoffs and a check

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_flow_11.90x3.90_f893b26e.png
objects.alt: Every workflow has four parts: a trigger, steps, handoffs and a check

objects.text: If you can name these four for a task, you can decide where AI fits.

slides.notes:
Every workflow, at work or at home, has four parts. A trigger starts it, such as a message arriving or the first Monday of the month. Then come the steps, in order. Then the handoffs, where work passes from one person or system to another. And finally the check, where somebody confirms the result is right.

Think of a hospital ward round: the trigger is a new patient, the steps are tests, the handoffs are between nurse and doctor, and the check is the doctor signing. Today you name these four for your own task.

title.text:
A mapped workflow: customer messages
at Nile Valley Foods in three lanes

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_t12_map_11.90x4.25.png
objects.alt: A mapped workflow: customer messages at Nile Valley Foods in three lanes

objects.text: One lane per person or team. Red arrows are handoffs: Customer Service waits for Finance.

slides.notes:
Here is a finished map from our case company. Each lane is a person or a team. The trigger, in red, is a customer message arriving. Customer Service reads and sorts it, then drafts a reply. When money is involved, the draft waits for Finance to confirm the payment: that handoff and its return are the red arrows.

Finally a person checks and sends. Draw your own map the same way: lanes for people, boxes for steps, arrows for handoffs. The handoffs are where you will find the waiting time.

title.text: Decide each step with four questions

rows.text: Is the answer fixed by clear words or numbers?
A payment reference goes to Finance
Does it need the meaning of text, with a quick check?
Sort a polite complaint; draft a reply
Does it need several tools and its own next step?
Read a mailbox and draft replies
Does money, trust or law turn on it?
Approve a credit; send the reply

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_calculator_0.50.png
/Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_robot_0.50.png
/Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_gear_0.50.png
/Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_person_0.50.png

objects.text: Ask the questions in this order. Use the first answer that fits.

slides.notes:
For each step on your map, ask four questions in order. Is the answer fixed by clear words or numbers?

Then use a rule, like a payment reference that always goes to Finance. Does it need the meaning of the text, and can a person check the result quickly?

Then an AI step. Does it need several tools and a choice of next step?

Then an agent, with the boundary sheet from Session 11. And whenever money, trust or the law turns on the step, a person decides. Use the first answer that fits.

title.text: The same map with a choice on every step

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_t12_map_11.90x4.25_3beb07f1.png
objects.alt: The same map with a choice on every step

objects.text: Two AI steps, one rule and a person at the end. No step here needs a full agent.

slides.notes:
This is the same map with a choice on each step. Reading and sorting is an AI step, because meaning matters: a polite complaint has no angry words. Drafting is an AI step too. Confirming a payment is a rule, because a payment reference is clear. Checking and sending stays with a person, because a reply commits the company.

Notice that no step needs a full agent. Most workflows need one or two AI steps inside a fixed path. An agent earns its place only when the steps change from case to case.

title.text:
Demonstration: the rule and the AI on
the same twelve customer messages

objects.text: I will show

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_flow_7.30x3.90_606a0631.png
objects.alt: Demonstration: the rule and the AI on the same twelve customer messages

objects.text: Watch for

runs.text: Which messages fool the rule?
Which one fools the AI?
What does UNSURE cost you?
What was never measured?

slides.notes:
Now the demonstration, from records we already have; nothing is rerun. The AI sort is a recorded run you see for the first time today (Session 2 only mentioned it). The rule is a simple keyword router I wrote after reading the twelve messages, so its seven flatters it.

The same twelve customer messages went through two automations. The rule router sends messages to queues by words: payment words to Finance, late or delay to Customer Service, everything else to the Sales desk. The AI sort reads the meaning and picks a category, or says UNSURE. Both are scored against the answer key.

Watch which messages fool the rule, which one fools the AI, and what the AI’s UNSURE answers cost a person.

title.text:
Side by side: the rule routes 7 of 12, the
AI sorts 9 exactly and 11 acceptably

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_t12_side_11.90x4.25.png
objects.alt: Side by side: the rule routes 7 of 12, the AI sorts 9 exactly and 11 acceptably

objects.text: AI: Claude, three fresh sessions, 4 November 2026; not ChatGPT or Gemini. Rule: computed.

slides.notes:
Here are the twelve, side by side. The rule gets seven right. It fails on M03, wet sugar with no keyword, on M10, a polite complaint, on M32, sarcastic thanks, and on M07 and M38, where late is part of an ordinary order. The AI, in three fresh Claude sessions on the fourth of November, gets nine exactly right and says UNSURE on two, which is acceptable.

It is wrong on M14, which it called a complaint while Finance must act first. The two counts use different measures, so read them side by side.

title.text:
Measure the baseline first: the saving is
the gap between today and the new way

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_t12_hours_7.70x4.80.png
objects.alt: Measure the baseline first: the saving is the gap between today and the new way

objects.text: Hours saved = times a month x minutes saved each time.

runs.text: 4 x 80 = 320 minutes, about 5.3 hours a month.
NVF Monday sales email: a plan with invented numbers.
Review time is a cost. Count it separately.

slides.notes:
Now the calculation, by hand. Take the Monday sales email at Nile Valley Foods. Today it takes ninety minutes. With the new routine the plan is ten minutes of your own work. So each run saves eighty minutes. It runs four times a month. Four times eighty is three hundred and twenty minutes, about five point three hours a month.

These are invented plan numbers from the workbook example. The twenty minutes of review is a cost and goes on the Costs sheet. Without a measured baseline, the saving is a guess.

title.text:
The Business Case Workbook turns those
hours into money: NVF plan example

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_t12_money_7.70x4.80.png
objects.alt: The Business Case Workbook turns those hours into money: NVF plan example

objects.text: Gains minus running cost gives the net a month.

runs.text: Time saved: 320 minutes at UGX 30,000 an hour.
Errors avoided: 4 runs x 40% x 60% x UGX 150,000.
Net UGX 159,000 a month. Set-up of UGX 480,000 pays back in 3.0 months.

slides.notes:
The workbook turns hours into money. These are the grey example values in the template, invented for Nile Valley Foods, and I recomputed them from the workbook’s own formulas. Time saved, 320 minutes at UGX 30,000 an hour, is UGX 160,000 a month. Errors avoided add UGX 144,000.

The running cost is UGX 145,000. So the net is UGX 159,000 a month, and the UGX 480,000 set-up pays back in about three months. Cut the benefit by thirty percent to be cautious and the year still ends positive.

title.text:
A personal assistant is a small workflow:
sketch its inputs, outputs and gate

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_t12_assistant_7.70x4.80.png
objects.alt: A personal assistant is a small workflow: sketch its inputs, outputs and gate

objects.text: Your own email is a good first workflow to map.

runs.text: Trigger: every morning at 7.
Badges: read one mailbox, write drafts.
Gate: you send every reply.

slides.notes:
Many executives would most like help with their own email. That is a workflow too. Sketch it like this. The trigger is the time, every morning at seven. The inputs are one mailbox and your rules, such as who counts as urgent. The outputs are a summary and draft replies.

The badges are read and draft, level two from Session 11. And the gate is you: it never sends, pays or deletes. If you prefer a work task, map that instead. The sketch is the same.

title.text:
Map your workflow: trigger,
steps, handoffs and check

objects.text: 15 minutes
Your own workflow
Draw one repeated task in lanes, from trigger to check.

runs.text: Pick one weekly task. Unsure? List options on the Use-Case Scorecard.
Draw one lane for each person or system.
Write the trigger, then each step in a box.
Mark every handoff in red and the check in gold.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_card_5.50x3.55_3557777c.png
objects.alt: What your finished page looks like

objects.text: You keep: A one-page map of your workflow with the handoffs marked.

slides.notes:
Now your own workflow. Pick one task you do every week. It can be a work task, such as the monthly report, supplier invoices or leave requests, or the summary of your own email. Draw a lane for each person or system involved. Write the trigger, then each step in a box.

Mark every handoff in red and the check in gold. If you cannot choose, list a few on the Ten tasks sheet of the Use-Case Scorecard: task, owner, how often, kind of work and minutes each time. Then fill the top of a Task Card. I come round and work with you. You have fifteen minutes.

title.text: Decide each step: rule, AI step, agent or person

objects.text: 15 minutes
Your own workflow
Tag every box on your map with one choice and one reason.

runs.text: Ask the four questions for each step, in order.
Write rule, AI step, agent or person in the box.
For each AI step, write how a person checks it.
Circle the step that costs the most time.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_sheet_5.50x3.55_251ccb84.png
objects.alt: What your finished page looks like

objects.text: You keep: Your map with a choice, a reason and a check on every step.

slides.notes:
Second step: decide. For every box on your map, ask the four questions in order. Clear words or numbers: a rule. Meaning with a quick check: an AI step. Several tools and its own next step: an agent. Money, trust or law: a person. Write the choice and one reason in the box.

For every AI step, write how a person checks it, because Session 10 showed us that models fail. Then circle the step that costs you the most time. That is usually where to start. Fifteen minutes.

title.text:
Sketch your personal assistant
with its badges and gate

objects.text: 10 minutes
Your own workflow
Draw one assistant for your workflow: inputs, outputs, badges, gate.

runs.text: Write its trigger and its inputs.
Write the outputs it hands to you.
Give it the fewest badges that work.
Name the gate and the off switch.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_sheet_5.50x3.55_a2536135.png
objects.alt: What your finished page looks like

objects.text: You keep: A sketch of one assistant with its four boundary rows.

slides.notes:
Third step, ten minutes. If one of your steps suits an assistant, sketch it. Write its trigger and its inputs, then the outputs it hands to you. Give it the fewest badges that still do the job, using the four rows of the Tool Boundary Sheet: read, write, send and spend.

Name the gate, the person who approves, and the off switch. If no step in your workflow suits an assistant, write that down. It is a useful finding. A rule or one AI step may be all you need.

title.text:
Estimate the hours saved and enter
them in the Business Case Workbook

objects.text: 15 minutes
Your own workflow
Fill the Inputs sheet for your workflow and read the hours saved.

runs.text: Type how often, minutes today and people involved.
Type minutes with the new routine and review minutes.
Add your hourly cost: pay plus contributions, over hours worked.
Mark each figure E for estimate or M for measured.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/x_sheet_5.50x3.55_177a7077.png
objects.alt: What your finished page looks like

objects.text: You keep: Your Inputs sheet filled, with the hours saved and every figure marked E or M.

slides.notes:
Last step, fifteen minutes. Open the Business Case Workbook and go to the Inputs sheet. Type over the grey example: times a month, minutes each time today, people involved, minutes with the new routine and review minutes. Never set review to zero. Work out your hourly cost: pay plus employer contributions and benefits, divided by hours worked.

Mark each figure E if it is your estimate and M if you measured it. The Benefits sheet then shows the hours saved. Most of your figures will be E today.

title.text:
Plan against measurement: four
numbers to record for four weeks

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_clock_0.70.png

objects.text: Minutes each run, with the new routine, including review.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_cross_0.70.png

objects.text: Errors found in each run, and what each cost.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_person_0.70.png

objects.text: Cases sent to a person, such as UNSURE.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_flag_0.70.png

objects.text: Your stop rule: the number at which you revise or stop.

slides.notes:
Your estimate is a plan. Before anyone spends money, measure four weeks of the real task with the new routine, using four numbers. Minutes each run, including the review. Errors found in each run, and what each cost. Cases sent to a person, such as the UNSURE answers we saw from the AI.

And your stop rule, written now while you are calm: for example, revise if review rises above thirty minutes a run. The workbook’s Stop rules sheet has examples. A measured result that beats the plan is your strongest case.

title.text: Decision: what will you build or test first?

objects.text: For your mapped workflow, which first step do you choose?

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_calculator_0.80.png

objects.text: A rule
Clear words or numbers. Cheap to build and easy to explain.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_robot_0.80.png

objects.text: One AI step
Meaning matters and a person checks each result.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_gear_0.80.png

objects.text: An assistant at level 2
Several steps; drafts only; you approve.

objects.path: /Users/jothamwambi/Projects/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/Applied AI and Automation - Executive Edition/05 Course Maintenance/Build/figures/icon_clock_0.80.png

objects.text: Measure first
No baseline yet. Time four weeks, then decide.
Write the step, your choice and the number that will tell you it worked.

slides.notes:
Now decide. For your mapped workflow, what do you build or test first?

A rule, when the words or numbers are clear: cheap to build and easy to explain. One AI step, when meaning matters and a person checks each result. An assistant at level two, when several steps change from case to case, with drafts only and you approving. Or measure first, when you have no baseline yet.

Say your choice aloud, then write the step, the choice and the number that will show it worked.

title.text: Keep your map and your hours-saved estimate

objects.text: What you keep from today

runs.text: Your mapped workflow, the choice for each step, your assistant sketch and the hours-saved estimate in the Business Case Workbook.

You keep your map, your choices, your assistant sketch and the workbook with your estimate. Your estimate is a plan. Before you trust it, measure four weeks of the real task. In Session 13 we write the policy and vendor questions around your map, so bring it with you.

We began with this question: Which of my tasks should be a rule, an AI step or an agent? Before you go, say in one sentence what you can now say about it.
